Q: How to document Vue Single-File Components that use the Composition API? A:

Took me a while to figure this one out...

Documenting Componenets

With the new recommended Composition-Api this is simply not possible, at least not by itself.

What gave me the idea was this part of the official vue documentation:
https://vuejs.org/api/sfc-script-setup.html#usage-alongside-normal-script

"<script setup> can be used alongside normal <script>" [...] to "declare options that cannot be expressed in ".

So is possible to use a <script> tag alongside <script setup> to extend the composition API with custom options and more.
We can (ab-)use this to document the Component, which is implemented in <script setup>.

  • Make sure that <script>-tag uses the same lang="ts" as <script setup>.
  • The comment will appear at the very bottom of the Hover-Tooltip in VSCode. This is annoying but at least it's there. Maybe someone else knows how to "fix" / change that.
  • Sometimes you may need to restart Vue: Restart Vue and TS servers with Ctrl + Shift + P.
  • I found that adding @class makes typedoc output more information about the component. You may find this helpful or simply be annoying boiler-plate. Up to you.
<script lang="ts">
/**
 * This comment will document the Component element itself.
 * 
 * @class
 */
export default {}
</script>

<script setup lang="ts">
// Your composition API component code.
</script>

Q: Calculating the true sample rate A:

I think I solved a bit of it.

  1. Get the address of where to start getting our data from GetBuffer(&buff, ...) (1st arg = BYTE* buff)

  2. store the first memory address (int* ptr = (int*)buff;)

  3. output the first memory address's value as a float (cout << *(float*)ptr << "\n";)

  4. move to the next memory address (ptr++)

  5. output the second memory address's value as a float (see 3.)

  6. repeat until you reach X (X should be the amount of available data - i'm not sure of this part yet)

Q: How to open a file from the integrated terminal in Visual Studio Code? A:

If your copy of visual studio code happens to be the codium build, you can use the following in the integrated terminal:

codium -r filename.txt
